texts.label: R9426, Ferdinand of Bavaria to Maximilian I, Bonn, 22 Dec 1619
texts.summary: Ferdinand of Bavaria, Elector of Cologne, writes to his brother Duke Maximilian I of Bavaria about quartering and paying the Catholic League's troops in the Rhine-Westphalian circle (Horn, Montfort, Deutz, Lintelo's and Herberstorff's companies, a year's respite for Paderborn), and argues that the common union is needed for the conservation of the Catholic religion. Six weeks after Frederick V's coronation in Prague; nomenclator groups apart from 248 = und are open.

reading_review.note: v3 verification 23 Oct 2026: reading.txt (one manuscript line per row, clear text in brackets, flagged words in capitals) scored 0.0, because the bracketed clear text counts as supplied words. Joined into running text in R9426_reading.md (clear text in «», flagged words lower case, eight unresolved flagged words as [?word], <nnn> open nomenclator groups as holes): 0.644 explicit-hole (58/90 sentences, hole rate 0.124); plain 0.311 (1619 German spelling). Marginal: the open nomenclator groups (<414>, <122> ...) fall in many sentences; the nomenclator is still open apart from 248 = und.

texts.label: R9425, Archduke Albert's resolution for Licentiate Morreus, 15 Dec 1619
texts.summary: Archduke Albert's written resolution for the League agent Licentiate Morreus: he agrees on the recovery of the kingdom of Bohemia, has done good offices with the Emperor and the King of Spain, will send troops on foot if needed but cannot grant the muster place, the regiment of foot and the 500 horse, and refers the 1000 cuirassiers to Ambrogio Spinola. Read with the R9426 key unchanged.

reading_review.note: r9425/reading.md is continuous German prose with scattered ⟨n⟩ code groups (Albert's answer to Morreus on the recovery of the Palatinate and the League's assistance); sentences build around the open groups.
